items.title: British couple on honeymoon killed in helicopter crash on Greek island
items.description: A young British couple and their pilot were killed in a helicopter crash on the Greek island of Sifnos on Monday, Greek police have said. They have been named as newlyweds Alexander Cromie and Marie Ebert, who were in Greece on their honeymoon. The private helicopter crashed just metres from a landing pad, killing the pair and their pilot, a Greek national. The couple are said to have taken the helicopter from the village of Markopoulo near Athens to the popular holiday island, Kathimerini reported. Greece’s aviation safety authority told the BBC it was investigating the crash and that its investigators were heading to the scene on Tuesday to gather evidence and speak to witnesses. The BBC has contacted the UK Foreign Office, the Greek authorities and the aviation company for comment. Asset management firm Blackstone, where Cromie worked, said in a statement: “We are shocked by the tragic passing of three people, including our colleague Alex Cromie and his wife Marie Ebert, who were celebrating their honeymoon. “Alex was beloved by everyone who knew and worked with him at Blackstone, and our thoughts and prayers are with his loved ones.” A senior police official told the Times that the crash came just before the helicopter’s scheduled landing time of 18:15 local time (16:15 GMT). Sifnos’ Deputy Mayor, Manolis Foundoulakis, arrived at the scene shortly after the incident and told local news site Newsit there was almost “nothing left” of the aircraft. He said locals saw the helicopter crash within metres of their homes and had described a “bizarre engine noise coming from the aircraft” as it was about to land. He said two of the victims were found in the wreckage, while the third was a short distance away. Firefighters worked to tackle a blaze which broke out after the crash, and the flames had been extinguished by Monday evening.

items.title: Tunisie: la Kharja de Sidi Bou Saïd, une procession qui réunit deux confréries soufies
items.description: En Tunisie, la Kharja de Sidi Bou Saïd, une procession soufie dans le village touristique, fait partie des traditions intégrées dans le classement du village de Sidi Bou Saïd au patrimoine mondial de l’Unesco le 25 juillet. Elle attire chaque mois d’août des centaines de curieux et des adeptes du soufisme. Lors de cette tradition islamique très ancienne, les confréries de l’Ariana, quartier de Tunis, et de Sidi Bou Saïd entament une procession mystique et de chants liturgiques qui durent trois jours, pendant qu'elles psalmodient ensemble.

items.title: Législatives en Israël: aux primaires du Likoud, Benyamin Netanyahu maintient son emprise sur le parti malgré l'incertitude
items.description: En Israël, une nuit décisive s’est jouée du lundi 17 au mardi 18 août, au stade de football de Jaffa, où les bulletins des primaires du Likoud ont été dépouillés jusqu’au petit matin. Dans un scrutin interne à haut risque, marqué par une forte abstention, 140 000 adhérents étaient appelés à recomposer la liste pour les prochaines élections législatives d'octobre. Dans le système israélien à la proportionnelle intégrale, chaque rang sur la liste vaut de l’or. D’autant que les places éligibles étaient particulièrement chères : entre les sièges réservés directement par Benyamin Netanyahu et la perspective d'un recul du parti au Parlement, plusieurs figures historiques risquaient l'éviction.

items.title: Zoundwéogo/Nobéré : la DRAERAH du Nazinon sollicite l’appui des autorités pour une mobilisation communautaire autour de la sécurité sanitaire de l’eau
items.description: BURKINA-ZOUNDWEOGO-SECURITE-SANITAIRE-EAU Zoundwéogo/Nobéré : la DRAERAH du Nazinon sollicite l’appui des autorités pour une mobilisation communautaire autour de la sécurité sanitaire de l’eau Nobéré, 13 août 2026 (AIB) – La Direction régionale de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques (DRAERAH) du Nazinon a rencontré, jeudi 13 août 2026, les autorités de la commune de Nobéré, en vue de solliciter leur accompagnement pour une mobilisation communautaire autour de la sécurité sanitaire de l’eau. Cette rencontre d’information et de plaidoyer visait notamment à sensibiliser les autorités locales sur les bonnes pratiques d’hygiène et d’assainissement, afin de contribuer à la préservation de la qualité de l’eau et à la protection de la santé des populations. La délégation était conduite par la cheffe du Service régional des ressources en eau et de l’hydraulique, Raboloum Ouédraogo Lalaïcha. Elle a expliqué aux participants les enjeux liés au plan de gestion de la sécurité sanitaire de l’eau initié par la direction régionale. Le président de la délégation spéciale (PDS) de Nobéré, le camarade Pierre Kafando, a salué l’initiative et appelé les participants à se faire les relais des bonnes pratiques d’hygiène et d’assainissement auprès des populations des quartiers et villages. Selon la Camarade Ouédraogo, le choix de Nobéré s’explique par la nécessité d’agir dans une commune confrontée à des préoccupations liées à la qualité de l’eau. « Nous sommes à Nobéré parce que la santé de nos populations est une priorité. Nous sollicitons votre accompagnement pour mobiliser massivement afin que le message atteigne chaque foyer », a-t-elle déclaré. Pour rappel, le forage d’adduction d’eau potable de la commune de Nobéré a été fermé en mars 2026, après que des analyses ont révélé un taux d’arsenic présenté comme étant 30 fois supérieur à la norme, selon la note de fermeture. La défécation à l’air libre ainsi que l’utilisation excessive de produits chimiques dans les activités aurifères sont notamment évoquées comme des causes probables de contamination. C’est dans cette perspective que la commune de Nobéré a été retenue pour cette campagne de mobilisation et de sensibilisation visant à contribuer à une meilleure gestion de la sécurité sanitaire de l’eau. Les autorités locales ont marqué leur adhésion à l’initiative. Le Dapoya Naaba, représentant le chef de canton, a salué une initiative « salvatrice » et assuré de son accompagnement pour favoriser un changement durable des comportements et l’amélioration du cadre de vie des populations. items.title: US lists 3 categories of visa services affected in Nigeria
items.description: The US Department of State has announced a realignment of routine visa services in Nigeria and several other African countries as part of a broader move to regional visa hubs. The US Mission in Nigeria disclosed the development in a visa services update, stating that routine visa operations in Abuja are among those being realigned. #FAQ : What type of visa services are being realigned? All routine nonimmigrant visa services, including tourist and business-related visas, and petition-based nonimmigrant visas. #VisaWiseTravelSmart pic.twitter.com/uK0AYBAWU7 — U.S. Mission Nigeria (@USinNigeria) August 18, 2026 The change affects applicants seeking nonimmigrant visas, including those travelling to the United States for tourism, business and other temporary purposes. Why the US is realigning visa services The US Department of State said the move is part of its efforts to strengthen national security, improve efficiency and ensure greater consistency in visa screening and adjudication. The department said the Trump administration is prioritising national security and the efficient use of government resources. It explained that the State Department regularly evaluates its overseas operations to ensure they advance US priorities while maintaining rigorous standards for security screening and vetting. According to the department, visa operations in Africa are being realigned to regional hubs as part of a long-standing practice that promotes more uniform screening, vetting and adjudication standards. The State Department said the regional hub system has already been implemented successfully in several African countries as well as in Europe. When does the change take effect? The realignment took effect on August 1, 2026, with routine visa services in Abuja and several other African cities being transferred to designated regional visa hubs. The affected locations include Abuja, as well as Antananarivo, Asmara, Bamako, Banjul, Brazzaville, Bujumbura, Conakry, Cotonou, Durban, Freetown, Gaborone, Harare, Juba, Libreville, Lilongwe, Lusaka, Maputo, Maseru, Mbabane, N’Djamena, Niamey, Nouakchott, Ouagadougou and Windhoek. Citizens and residents of the affected countries who wish to apply for a US visa must schedule their appointments and pay the required visa fees at the appropriate designated visa location. Which visa services are affected? The realignment covers routine visa services, including: Tourist visa applications Business-related visa applications Petition-based nonimmigrant visas Nonimmigrant visas are generally issued to people seeking temporary entry into the United States for purposes including tourism, business, study, work and other approved activities. What does this mean for Nigerian applicants? Nigerians applying for US visas from Abuja may now have to use a designated regional visa hub for their applications, depending on the type of visa and the applicant’s circumstances. Applicants are advised to check the latest instructions from the US Mission and the US Department of State before scheduling appointments or making visa payments. The State Department has also stressed that the realignment is intended to maintain rigorous security screening and vetting standards while improving the efficiency of its visa operations. items.title: Man, 20, drowns while helping travellers cross Ghana-Togo border river
items.description: A 20-year-old man, identified as Kombat Yaw Yiremiah, has drowned in a river separating Ghana and Togo at Tambalug in the Tempane District of the Upper East Region. The tragedy occurred around 10:30 a.m. on Sunday, August 16, 2026. Kombat Yaw Yiremiah was reportedly assisting travellers to cross the river. As of close of day on Monday (August 17, 2026) his body had not been found. Community members, relatives and personnel of the National Disaster Management Organisation (NADMO) are engaged in a search. Helping travellers turns tragic According to the family, Yiremiah and some of his colleagues regularly assisted travellers, including Togolese nationals and people arriving from Kumasi, Accra, Bolgatanga and Tamale, to cross the river into Togo or vice versa. The young man had reportedly gone about his usual activity on Sunday when the tragedy struck. What started as an ordinary day of helping people navigate the river suddenly turned into a desperate search for his own life. The Tempane District Director of NADMO, George Alale Akuka, confirmed that his team had been involved in the search for the missing young man’s body. He said the search team had covered a considerable distance along the river but had, as of Monday afternoon, not been able to locate the body. Mr Akuka described the situation as serious, saying the team was continuing its efforts to locate and recover the body. “So myself and my team, we are still on the ground searching for him,” he added. Traditional intervention The NADMO Director also disclosed that traditional considerations had become part of the recovery efforts, explaining that the community had consulted people who had previously been involved in locating victims in similar circumstances. He said the team had been informed that, following the traditional consultation, there was confidence that the body could be located. “They consulted the one who used to consult the gods before they see the victim, so they get the direction, and we are confident that in about a few hours from now, we will get him,” he said. Mr Akuka, however, stressed that he and his team remained on the ground and would continue to monitor the situation. Family appeal Following the incident, the family and residents appealed to the Ghana Police Service and NADMO to provide the necessary support to recover the body. They said professional rescue personnel and appropriate equipment were needed to conduct the search safely and effectively, particularly because of the difficult conditions at the river. Community in shock The incident has left the family and the Tambalug community devastated, particularly because Yiremiah was reportedly helping people cross the border river when he drowned. The community is, therefore, appealing to the authorities to act swiftly to support the search and help bring closure to the grieving family. As the search continues, the family remains anxiously waiting for the recovery of the body of their son.

items.title: Les entreprises qui résistent à Trump ne sont pas pénalisées par les marchés
items.description: Selon une étude publiée le 14 août par deux chercheurs des universités Stanford et Berkeley, les entreprises qui n’ont pas modifié leurs politiques de diversité, d'équité et d'inclusion (DEI) à la suite du décret promulgué par Donald Trump le 21 janvier 2025, soit le lendemain de son retour au pouvoir, n’ont pas subi d’effets négatifs sur les marchés, mais elles ont même surperformé par rapport à celles qui se sont conformées aux nouvelles directives de la Maison-Blanche Markets Do Not Punish Firms for Maintaining DEI », 14 août 2026.'> 1 . Le décret n°14173, intitulé « Mettre fin à la discrimination illégale et restaurer les opportunités fondées sur le mérite », fait partie des 42 signés par Trump dans les 10 premiers jours de son nouveau mandat. Il ordonne aux agences fédérales de mettre fin à tous leurs programmes DEI internes, et mandate l'investigation des programmes DEI dans le secteur privé, avec possibilité de poursuites contre les entreprises et les universités qui les maintiennent. Selon Folsz et Grumbach, l’étude des « retours anormaux » – c'est-à-dire la différence entre les performances attendues d’une action boursière et ses performances réelles – démontre que le décret n’a pas pénalisé les entreprises qui ne s’y sont pas conformées, que ce soit en termes de rendements boursiers ou de chiffre d’affaires. Ces résultats soulignent les limites du slogan « go woke, go broke » (« le wokisme conduit à la faillite »), popularisé durant la campagne de 2024 et utilisé par des influenceurs conservateurs pour exercer une pression sur les entreprises jugées trop progressistes. De grandes sociétés, dont certaines avaient abandonné leurs programmes DEI à la suite du décret, ont depuis fait l’objet d’enquêtes du département de la Justice pour utilisation détournée du False Claims Act. C’est notamment le cas de Google et de Verizon, visés par l’administration Trump pour avoir pris en compte des critères de diversité lors du recrutement alors qu'ils détiennent des contrats avec le gouvernement fédéral – ce qui pourrait, selon cette interprétation, constituer un cas de « fraude » Justice Department Using Fraud Law to Target Companies on DEI », The Wall Street Journal, 28 décembre 2025.'> 2 . Les politiques destinées à dissuader les entreprises américaines de prendre en compte des critères de diversité, mises en place par l’administration républicaine, ont conduit à une baisse des nominations de femmes et de personnes issues de minorités. Leur part parmi les nouveaux administrateurs nommés par les entreprises du S&P 500 a atteint cette année son niveau le plus bas depuis 2014. Ainsi, sur les 364 nouveaux administrateurs indépendants nommés entre mai 2025 et avril 2026, seulement 40 % étaient des femmes ou des personnes issues de minorités, contre 72 % en 2022 Trump's diversity crackdown reverberates through US boardrooms », Reuters , 28 juillet 2026.'> 3 . Seulement 12 % des entreprises du S&P 500 déclarent désormais prendre en compte des critères de diversité dans leurs décisions relatives aux conseils d’administration, soit quatre fois moins qu’en 2024 (48 %). L’article Les entreprises qui résistent à Trump ne sont pas pénalisées par les marchés est apparu en premier sur Le Grand Continent .

items.title: Fire destroys more than 27 wooden structures at Spintex Coastal junction
items.description: A fire outbreak at Spintex Coastal junction has destroyed more than 27 wooden structures following an incident that occurred early Tuesday morning. According to ADO I Kojo Poku, who reported from the scene, the fire started at about 6:20 a.m. and quickly spread through the wooden structures, resulting in extensive destruction. More than 27 structures, along with their contents, were destroyed before firefighters managed to bring the blaze under control. The Ghana National Fire Service (GNFS) responded with two fire appliances deployed from nearby fire stations. A private water tanker also supported the operation by supplying additional water to sustain firefighting efforts. After several hours of operations, firefighters eventually extinguished the fire at about 9:22 a.m. One church and an adjoining building were also affected by the fire. The cause of the fire has not yet been established. The GNFS has urged the public to observe fire safety measures, take necessary precautions and report fire outbreaks immediately when detected.

items.title: GoldBod: Day of reckoning will come – Afenyo-Markin
items.description: Minority Leader and Effutu MP Alexander Afenyo-Markin has warned that those responsible for what he describes as financial losses at the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) will eventually be held accountable. Speaking at a Minority press conference in Parliament on Tuesday, August 18, Mr Afenyo-Markin said the Minority would not be intimidated by attacks on the personalities of those raising concerns about GoldBod’s operations. He maintained that GoldBod must account for what he described as a GH¢22 billion loss involving the institution, arguing that the alleged loss amounted to causing financial loss to the state. “So they must account for the GH¢22 billion loss. It must account for it because it amounts to causing financial loss to the state,” he said. Mr Afenyo-Markin said the Minority would continue to raise the issue firmly and without fear, regardless of the response from GoldBod officials. “It doesn’t matter the adjectives that they use to describe or to attack our personalities, and we know the day of reckoning will come,” he said. He stressed that the Minority’s position was rooted in its responsibility to scrutinise the management of public resources and demand accountability from state institutions. His comments come amid a dispute between the Minority and GoldBod management over the institution’s financial performance, with GoldBod rejecting claims that it has incurred losses.

items.title: Osun Election: ‘When they lose, FG manipulated; but when they win…’ – Wike
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, said on Tuesday in Abuja that whenever the opposition loses election, they accuse the Federal Government of manipulation, but show off wins. Read Also: Abuja flooding: All houses on water channels will go down, Wike vows Wike made the statement in reference to the just-concluded Osun State governorship election, adding that President Bola Tinubu’s administration should be commended for allowing processes to run of their own without interference. Furthermore, Wike said the 2027 presidential election will be the easiest contest for President Bola Tinubu, describing Nigeria’s opposition as “crippled and depleted.” Asked about his reaction to the outcome of last Saturday’s Governorship Election in Osun state which was won by the opposition, Wike credited the current administration for allowing democratic processes to run without interference, contrasting it with the tension that surrounded the 2023 election. “2023 was a tough election for him. Nobody knew what the government at the time was trying to do, and even governors were afraid,” he said, adding that unpredictability would not define 2027. “When they lose, they claim the government manipulated the process; when they win, they show off their might. It does not work that way. “From what I have seen, this government allows processes to run their own way, and they must be given credit for that”, he added. The minister said unseating an incumbent requires a strong, vibrant opposition built over years, not one still searching for direction. “To remove a government, you need a strong, vibrant opposition that has spent over four years planning, not one that is constantly looking for a party to join,” he said. He singled out leaders of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, for internal divisions and weak showings in recent governorship polls, arguing that the coordinated support of the G5 governors that shaped the 2023 race would not be replicated nationally in 2027. “Governorship elections rely on local variables, but a national election is a completely different ballgame. If it is this 2027 election against Bola Ahmed Tinubu, forget it. It is over,” he said. On economic discontent, Wike urged Nigerians to judge leadership by concrete actions rather than sentiments. “Leadership is defined by the steps you take to solve problems. When someone identifies a problem and takes concrete action to fix it, that is the effort people should appreciate,” he said. items.title: Élections 2026 : L’UNICEF appelle les partis politiques à faire des droits de l’enfant une priorité
items.description: À l’approche des élections législatives et du renouvellement de la Chambre des représentants ainsi que du futur gouvernement marocain, le Fonds des Nations unies pour l’enfance (UNICEF) exhorte les acteurs politiques à faire des droits de l’enfant une priorité des programmes électoraux et de l’action publique à venir. Dans un appel publié le 17 août 2026, l’organisation rappelle que les enfants, bien qu’ils ne participent pas au scrutin, demeurent directement concernés par les choix politiques effectués aujourd’hui. « Les enfants ne participent pas au vote, mais les décisions prises aujourd’hui façonneront leur avenir ainsi que celui du Maroc pour les décennies à venir », souligne l’UNICEF. L’agence onusienne insiste sur le poids démographique de cette catégorie de la population. Représentant près d’un tiers des habitants du Royaume, les enfants constituent, selon elle, un levier stratégique pour accélérer le développement humain, renforcer la cohésion sociale et soutenir une prospérité durable. Des progrès reconnus, mais des défis persistants L’UNICEF met en avant les avancées enregistrées par le Maroc au cours de la dernière décennie en matière de protection de l’enfance. L’organisation cite notamment l’extension de la couverture sociale, les réformes structurelles engagées dans les secteurs de la santé et de l’éducation, le lancement de programmes intégrés de développement territorial ainsi que le renforcement du cadre politique et juridique dédié à la protection des enfants. Ces acquis, estime-t-elle, ne doivent toutefois pas occulter l’ampleur des défis qui subsistent. Chaque année, environ 8.000 nouveau-nés meurent avant d’atteindre l’âge d’un mois, rappelle l’organisation. Les difficultés se manifestent également dans le domaine de l’éducation. Plus de 276.000 élèves ont quitté les bancs de l’école au cours de l’année scolaire 2024-2025. Dans le même temps, près de 103.000 enfants âgés de 7 à 17 ans demeuraient exposés au travail des enfants. À ces problématiques s’ajoutent les effets croissants du changement climatique. Selon l’UNICEF, quelque 6,9 millions d’enfants subissent de manière de plus en plus marquée les conséquences du stress hydrique et des dérèglements climatiques. Accélérer l’investissement en faveur de l’enfance Face à cette situation, l’organisation estime qu’il est nécessaire d’accélérer les efforts afin de garantir à chaque enfant, quel que soit son lieu de résidence, un accès effectif à des services de qualité et une pleine bénéficience des politiques publiques mises en œuvre. À l’horizon 2030, date fixée pour l’atteinte des Objectifs de développement durable, l’UNICEF considère que les prochaines années constitueront une période décisive pour renforcer les investissements destinés à l’enfance et traduire les ambitions du Nouveau Modèle de Développement en résultats tangibles pour les jeunes générations. Dans cette perspective, l’organisation indique avoir mis à la disposition des différents acteurs un ensemble de propositions opérationnelles couvrant plusieurs domaines prioritaires : la santé, l’éducation, l’inclusion sociale, la protection de l’enfance ainsi que le renforcement de la résilience face au changement climatique. Selon l’UNICEF, ces recommandations reposent sur des données et des analyses documentées. Elles visent à accompagner l’élaboration et la mise en œuvre de politiques publiques capables de consolider les acquis, de répondre aux défis persistants et de produire des résultats durables au bénéfice de chaque enfant au Maroc. items.title: Privatisations : pourquoi les 9 milliards de dirhams prévus en 2025 ne sont pas arrivés
items.description: Les 9 milliards de dirhams inscrits dans la loi de finances 2025 au titre des opérations sur le portefeuille public n’ont finalement pas été mobilisés. Si aucune opération de privatisation n’a été réalisée durant l’exercice, le rapport d’activité de la Direction des Entreprises Publiques et de la Privatisation (DEPP) met surtout en lumière une année consacrée à la refonte du cadre juridique, à la restructuration des entreprises publiques et à la préparation d’une nouvelle approche de gestion du portefeuille de l’État. Sur le papier, l’ambition était clairement affichée. La loi de finances 2025 avait prévu une recette globale de 9 milliards de dirhams, dont 6 milliards au titre des opérations de privatisation et 3 milliards correspondant à des cessions d’actifs ou à des opérations entre entités publiques. Au terme de l’exercice, le bilan dressé par la DEPP est sans ambiguïté : aucune opération de privatisation n’a été réalisée. Pour autant, le rapport ne décrit pas une année blanche en matière de portefeuille public. Il fait apparaître un chantier d’une autre nature, davantage tourné vers la préparation et la transformation du dispositif devant encadrer les futures opérations. L’un des éléments les plus significatifs concerne précisément le régime juridique de la privatisation. La DEPP indique que 2025 a été marquée par le suivi de l’examen d’un projet de réforme du cadre juridique applicable aux opérations de privatisation, de capital et de portefeuille. Les projets de textes législatifs et réglementaires élaborés dans ce cadre ont été transmis au ministère de l’Économie et des Finances ainsi qu’à l’Agence nationale de gestion stratégique des participations de l’État et de suivi des performances des établissements et entreprises publics (ANGSPE), pour examen et avis. Le calendrier donne une indication supplémentaire sur l’état d’avancement de ce chantier. Deux instances — un comité de suivi et un comité de pilotage — se sont réunies les 15 et 23 juillet 2025 pour examiner les projets de textes et procéder à leur finalisation. Cette séquence juridique s’inscrit dans une réforme plus large du secteur des établissements et entreprises publics. La DEPP précise que le cadre juridique et réglementaire de cette réforme était encore en cours de consolidation en 2025, avec des concertations accélérées avec les différents partenaires afin de parachever le dispositif. Le rapport recense ainsi neuf textes adoptés, deux textes en circuit d’adoption et six autres en cours de finalisation. Le contexte permet ainsi de mieux comprendre le décalage entre la prévision budgétaire et l’exécution. Le rapport ne présente pas explicitement la réforme juridique comme la cause directe de l’absence de privatisation. Il montre toutefois que l’année 2025 a été largement mobilisée par la préparation du nouveau cadre applicable aux opérations de privatisation, de capital et de portefeuille, parallèlement au chantier de restructuration des EEP. Cette restructuration constitue d’ailleurs l’un des axes majeurs de la réforme. La DEPP indique qu’un programme global d’opérations a été identifié, regroupant à la fois des opérations déjà engagées ou présentant un niveau de maturité élevé et d’autres encore en phase d’évaluation et de concertation. L’objectif porte notamment sur la transformation de certains EEP et la révision de leur modèle économique et financier. Le portefeuille n’est donc pas resté immobile. En 2025, la DEPP a accompagné la notification de 24 décrets, dont 11 portant création de filiales et 12 concernant des prises de participation. Parmi les nouvelles structures figurent notamment Noor Atlas Energy Company, West Med Container Terminal, OCP Nutricorps, Mzinda Fertilisers 1, 2 et 3 et OCP RE. Le mouvement est révélateur d’une transformation plus large de la gestion du portefeuille public. Alors que certaines entreprises figuraient sur la liste des entités privatisables — notamment Marsa Maroc, Maroc Telecom, La Mamounia, Énergie Électrique de Tahaddart, BIOPHARMA et SONACOS — l’année 2025 a parallèlement vu la constitution de nouvelles filiales et l’évolution de participations publiques. La réorganisation de la DEPP elle-même va dans le même sens. Entrée en vigueur en 2025, elle vise à renforcer les fonctions d’évaluation, de gouvernance, de gestion des risques et de suivi de la performance du portefeuille public. Cette évolution doit permettre d’accompagner une gestion davantage structurée des participations de l’État. items.description: Le president malien de la Transition, Assimi Goïta, a recu les 82 militaires liberes le 13 août dernier, lors d'une ceremonie organisee le 17 août dans la salle de banquets du palais Koulouba en presence du ministre delegue a la Defense, le general Oumar Diarra, et du chef d'etat-major general des Armees, le general elisee Jean Dao, en plus de plusieurs autres hauts responsables militaires et gouvernementaux. S'exprimant au nom de ses camarades liberes, le colonel Adama Bakayoko a fait part de ses remerciements et de sa reconnaissance au president et a l'ensemble de ses equipes pour les efforts consentis pour leur liberation. S'adressant aussi au chef d'etat-major et au ministre de la Defense, il les a salues pour leurs conseils avises et les dotations completes mises a leur disposition des leur liberation, exprimant son emotion et celle de ses camarades, ainsi que leur disposition a regagner le front, affirmant qu'« aucune portion du territoire national ne sera cedee ». Il en a egalement appele au soutien de la population aux Forces armees dans la defense de la souverainete malienne. Aucune negociation n'avait ete engagee avec l'ennemi Pour sa part, le general elisee Jean Dao a assure le soutien de la nation aux militaires, saluant leur resilience, leur tenacite et leur bravoure tout au long de leur detention, louant aussi leur volonte constante de rejoindre leurs camarades d'armes. Selon le chef d'etat-major, aucune negociation n'avait ete engagee avec l'ennemi, indiquant que les conditions avaient ete reunies pour que la detention de ces otages devienne intenable pour les groupes terroristes. Ces efforts, a-t-il rappele, ont ete menes sur instruction du chef de l'etat, determine a tout mettre en œuvre pour obtenir la liberation de l'ensemble des militaires retenus en captivite. Un engagement qui, a-t-il assure, se poursuit sans relâche. Ramener tous les militaires detenus ou portes disparus Le ministre de la Defense a mene un entretien avec la presse a l'issue de la ceremonie ou il a salue la bravoure et la dignite des militaires liberes, insistant sur la determination des autorites a n'abandonner aucun membre des Forces armees, malgre les difficultes rencontrees au cours des missions sur le terrain. Selon Oumar Diarra, l'objectif du gouvernement reste le meme : ramener tous les soldats maliens detenus ou portes disparus. Pour rappel, les 82 militaires maliens etaient retenus en otage par la coalition terroriste JNIM-FLA. a leur liberation, les militaires ont ete recus par le chef d'etat-major general des Armees, qui a assure la prise en charge par l'etat de leur suivi medical et du rattrapage des avantages perdus durant leur periode de captivite.

items.title: CSA fines EY Ghana GH¢360,000 for providing cybersecurity services without a licence
items.description: The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) has imposed a GH¢360,000 administrative penalty on Ernst & Young (EY) Ghana for providing regulated cybersecurity services without the requisite licence. The Authority said EY Ghana continued to provide regulated cybersecurity services, including services to owners of Critical Information Infrastructure (CII), despite directives to regularise its operations. In a statement dated August 18, 2026, the CSA said it directed EY Ghana on March 20, 2026, to submit an application for a Cybersecurity Service Provider (CSP) licence within 15 days. However, the Authority subsequently determined that the firm had failed to comply with three separate regulatory directives. The CSA said the conduct constitutes breaches of Sections 49 and 92 of the Cybersecurity Act, 2020 (Act 1038), which regulate the provision of cybersecurity services and provide sanctions for non-compliance. Under Sections 49(2), 92(2) and 93 of Act 1038, the CSA imposed a penalty of 10,000 penalty units, equivalent to GH¢120,000, for each of the three instances of non-compliance. This brings the total administrative penalty imposed on EY Ghana to GH¢360,000. The firm has been directed to pay the penalty within 14 calendar days from the date of the final enforcement directive. The CSA has also directed EY Ghana to immediately cease providing all regulated cybersecurity services without the required licence. The directive specifically includes Governance, Risk and Compliance (GRC) services. EY Ghana has further been ordered to provide written confirmation to the CSA that the affected services have ceased and complete the application process for a CSP licence. The Authority stressed that merely applying for a licence does not authorise a service provider to operate. “An application for a licence does not confer a licence to operate,” the CSA said, emphasising that providers must obtain the requisite licence before offering regulated cybersecurity services. The enforcement action has also been accompanied by a warning to other cybersecurity service providers operating in Ghana without the required licence. The CSA said compliance was particularly important where cybersecurity services are provided to owners of Critical Information Infrastructure, whose systems are essential to national security, the economy and the delivery of critical services. “The Authority therefore makes clear that the size, reputation, expertise or clientele of a service provider does not exempt it from Ghana’s cybersecurity laws,” the statement said. The Authority said all cybersecurity service providers are subject to the same regulatory requirements under Act 1038 and its directives. It has therefore directed unlicensed operators to cease providing regulated services and regularise their operations. The CSA also warned that it would continue monitoring compliance and take enforcement action against both unlicensed service providers and institutions that engage them. Such action, it said, could include administrative sanctions, court proceedings and publication of the names of unlicensed service providers where permitted by law. The Authority urged organisations, particularly owners of Critical Information Infrastructure, to ensure that cybersecurity services are procured only from appropriately licensed providers. “The message is clear: cybersecurity licensing is a legal requirement, not an administrative formality. Institutions must comply, and service providers must be licensed before they operate,” the CSA said. The latest enforcement action forms part of the Authority’s broader regulatory efforts to strengthen cybersecurity compliance and protect Ghana’s digital infrastructure and sensitive information.

items.title: Bonsu Baah scores and assists in Al Qadsiah big win in Saudi King’s Cup
items.description: Ghana international Christopher Bonsu Baah opened his scoring account for the 2026/27 season in Al Qadsiah’s big win in the Saudi King’s Cup. The Black Stars forward started in his side’s big win over Al Tai on Monday evening in what was his second appearance of the campaign. Italian forward Mateo Retegui opened the scoring for Al Qadsiah in the 16th minute before Bonsu Baah doubled the lead in the 34th minute. The Ghanaian pounced on a loose ball in the penalty box before dropping two players and the goalkeeper to score from close range. Just before the break, the Ghanaian also set up Retegui for his second goal of the opening half to make it 3-0 for Brendan Rodgers’ side. Al Qadsiah came back from recess and scored two more goals as they recorded a 5-0 away win over their opponents. Bonsu Baah played no minutes during the Black Stars’ 2026 World Cup campaign in Mexico, Canada and the United States of America as they crashed out in the Round of 32.

items.title: Nazinon/IPO: « À partir du moment où vous quittez ce site, vous devenez des ambassadeurs », le ministre Jean Marie Traoré
items.description: BURKINA-NAZINON-IPO-VISITE-MAE Nazinon/IPO: « À partir du moment où vous quittez ce site, vous devenez des ambassadeurs », le ministre Jean Marie Traoré Manga, 16 août 2026 (AIB)-Le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, a appelé, dimanche à Manga, les jeunes appelés à l’immersion patriotique obligatoire à devenir des ambassadeurs des valeurs patriotiques à l’issue de leur séjour, les exhortant à être « des filles et des fils du pays dignes, fiers, intègres et qui portent toujours avec fierté les étendards de leur pays ». Le chef de la diplomatie burkinabè s’exprimait lors d’une visite sur les sites d’immersion patriotique du lycée professionnel régional de Manga et du lycée provincial Naaba Baongo. « À partir du moment où vous quittez ce site, vous devenez des ambassadeurs », a déclaré le Camarade Ministre, invitant les appelés à transmettre les valeurs acquises à leurs familles, à leurs proches et, demain, dans les universités et les milieux professionnels qu’ils fréquenteront. Pour lui, le patriotisme ne doit pas se limiter aux discours, mais se traduire dans le savoir-être et les actes au quotidien. « On doit sentir le Burkina Faso, non pas seulement dans les discours, mais dans votre savoir-être, dans ce que vous faites, dans ce que vous êtes », a-t-il insisté. Sous une pluie battante, la délégation ministérielle est allée au contact des 462 appelés du site du lycée professionnel régional et des 293 appelées du lycée provincial Naaba Baongo. La visite avait pour objectif de s’enquérir des conditions de vie et d’apprentissage des immergés et de les encourager à s’investir pleinement dans cette expérience citoyenne, afin de s’approprier les principes et valeurs qui leur sont enseignés. La délégation a échangé avec les appelés et les équipes d’encadrement, avant de visiter les locaux et de partager un repas avec les jeunes. Sur les deux sites, le ministre et sa délégation ont constaté l’engagement des appelés ainsi que le dévouement des équipes d’encadrement, mobilisés pour faire de l’immersion un cadre d’apprentissage, de partage et de consolidation de l’esprit patriotique et de l’attachement à la nation. « Nous repartons avec une fierté renforcée, parce que nous avons vu des bacheliers qui sont totalement transformés du fait de l’encadrement et du séjour qu’ils ont passé ensemble. Les interactions entre appelés et entre appelés et encadreurs ont permis de renforcer l’esprit de civisme et leur lien avec la patrie », a déclaré Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré. Il a félicité les jeunes, les équipes d’encadrement et les autorités régionales pour leur mobilisation en faveur de la réussite de l’initiative. A cette occasion, le ministre a rappelé le message du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, selon lequel « les nations se construisent dans l’ordre, la discipline et sur les convictions patriotiques ». La région du Nazinon compte quatre sites d’encadrement accueillant au total 2 074 appelés dans le cadre de l’immersion patriotique obligatoire, au titre de l’année 2026. La visite s’est achevée par une plantation d’arbres. Agence d’information du Burkina Source : MAE

items.title: Alan Dershowitz Won’t Forget What Larry David Did to Him
items.description: H ere it is , August on Martha’s Vineyard, and Alan Dershowitz has barely been heard from. Well, that’s not exactly true. He has been heard from on many topics—because Dershowitz is who he is, and pretty much anyone can join Substack, and TV bookers can be hard to resist. Still, he has said little publicly about the maddening injustice he’s faced in recent years: his annual summer shunning at the hands of the island’s liberal social gentry. Has this perennial comedy of ill manners—the Vineyard cancellation of Alan Dershowitz—finally run its course? The story has become a familiar seasonal menace; as pernicious as ticks, and as hard to kill. Its particulars are known. Dershowitz, the inexhaustible Harvard Law professor who represented a gallery of notorious clients over several decades, was once a kibitzing dynamo here. But that was before the blacklists and the badgering. In his telling (and retelling), Dershowitz became socially radioactive during Donald Trump’s first term, when he began speaking out on the president’s behalf, and then joined his first impeachment defense team. Although he did not personally support Trump—he’d been a lifelong Democrat who’d voted for Hillary Clinton in 2016 and would support Joe Biden in 2020—his stock explanation was that everyone is entitled to legal representation. It was the same basic principle he had applied when representing the likes of Mike Tyson, O. J. Simpson, Claus von Bülow, and, more recently, Jeffrey Epstein. It was no different, in fact, than the occasion of Dershowitz’s first-ever visit to Martha’s Vineyard, in 1969, when he was enlisted to help in the defense of Ted Kennedy after his late-night accident at Chappaquiddick. Yet defending Trump was apparently too noxious for Dershowitz’s reputation. “I never thought I would see McCarthyism come to Martha’s Vineyard,” he lamented in a column in The Hill in 2018. According to Dershowitz, locals have urged his exclusion from various Vineyard businesses and institutions. Every summer, it seems, has brought a new episode in ostracism, cold shoulders in the hot sun. [ Thomas Chatterton Williams: The right is changing the rules of the culture war ] There was the Great Pierogi Incident last year at the West Tisbury farmers’ market, in which a vendor refused to sell half a dozen dumplings to Dershowitz, citing his representation of “several sexual predators and abusers, including Jeffrey Epstein.” Dershowitz claimed that he was being discriminated against over his vocal support for Israel and initiated a follow-up spectacle a week later in which the vendor, Krem Miskevich, refused to accept a signed copy of one of Dershowitz’s books ( The Ten Big Anti-Israel Lies ) as a peace offering. In 2022, Dershowitz said he’d received a fan email from a reader who alleged that he’d been beaten up at the beach (he did not specify where) just for carrying a copy of a book written by Dershowitz. “Without warning, I was slugged and punched in the face,” the man wrote to Dershowitz, who reprinted the unverified email on Substack in a post titled “Email From a Man Who Got Beaten Up for Reading My Book.” And then there was the infamous clash at the Chilmark General Store with Dershowitz’s now very-much-ex-friend Larry David. In the annals of Dershowitz’s social spiral on the Vineyard, this conflagration has taken on almost-mythic dimensions, like his own personal Stalingrad. Dershowitz was sitting on the porch of the store with another friend, “who happened to be a very kind of radical woke lefty from New York, but very tolerant,” he told me. David was not very tolerant, at least of Dershowitz. He walked onto the porch, refused to shake Dershowitz’s hand, called him “disgusting,” and stormed off. Dershowitz said at the time that David was so irate, Dershowitz worried that the comedian might suffer a stroke. That unpleasantness on the porch, memorialized on Page Six , took place five summers ago. But Dershowitz talks about it as if it were yesterday. On a recent Saturday, I ventured north from Washington for a little hardship duty in Chilmark, the preciously pastoral town on the western side of the island where Dershowitz has owned a home since 1991. I approached him first by email, telling Dershowitz that I was curious about his current social standing on the Vineyard and how things were going for him this summer. The subject matter could be freshly topical, I figured, because his two most prominent clients—Trump and Epstein—are more toxic than ever. To my surprise, Dershowitz agreed to speak with me. Actually, I was not surprised. “W e can meet on the porch for a slice,” he proposed. Dershowitz, who turns 88 next month, has been presiding from the rocking chairs of the Chilmark General Store for decades, juggling pizza and discourse. When I arrived, I found him wearing a bright-red T-shirt with the words Proud American over an Israeli flag and an American one, each in the shape of a heart. He told me that he’d asked his wife, Carolyn Cohen, to join us but she had no interest. “She said, ‘I’m so sick and tired of this subject,’” he told me. Dershowitz conceded that he, too, is weary of it. “But, you know, it’s important that people get the whole context,” he said. The whole context, in 2026, is basically this: Dershowitz says he has started a new life on the Vineyard. But just because his persecution tale has become an island eye-roll does not mean that it has subsided. Especially, according to Dershowitz, in his own, bucolic neighborhood. “Here in Chilmark, it’s 90 percent negative,” Dershowitz reported to me. That reception contrasts with what he gets in Miami Beach, where he spends his winters and where, he said, he is treated “wonderfully.” He is “treated very well” even in the more heavily trafficked Vineyard towns on the other side of the island. “In Edgartown and even Oak Bluffs, the African American community, I’m treated very well,” he said. “It’s all Chilmark. And it’s all Jewish, anti-Zionist.” I noted that he can at least still hold court at the Chilmark General Store. But he argued with my choice of the term holding court . “I used to—not anymore,” he said. “You don’t hold court anymore?” I asked, as he arguably held court. “What is this?” “You’re interviewing me,” he said. In the past, it would have been a high-end conclave. “Normally, we would have this whole area,” he said, motioning to a group of rocking chairs on one side of the porch. “I would have Larry David here,” he said. “Ted Danson was here sometimes,” he added. “The guy who did Ghostbusters —he died a few years ago—he was here.” (This was Harold Ramis, who died in 2014.) “The whole crew of Chilmark friends, I would say, 20 or so, no longer talk to me,” Dershowitz said. He pointed next door to the Chilmark Tavern, one of his favorite restaurants on the Vineyard, where he claims that some of his vacation nemeses are trying to get him banned. “A bunch of people went to the Chilmark Tavern and said If you continue to serve Dershowitz, we’re not coming here ,” he insisted. I was skeptical of this. “Ask her; you can check with her,” he said. “Jenny.” When I contacted Jenna Petersiel, the proprietor of the Chilmark Tavern, she told me that she’d assumed that The Atlantic wanted to speak with her about the challenges of running a restaurant, or ticks. “A discussion of Alan Dershowitz had not crossed my mind,” she said, declining to comment otherwise. Dershowitz also told me of an event he had attended on the Chilmark Tavern deck not long ago. A woman got out of her car, he claimed, “saw I was up there, turned around, and went back to her car.” He appears to have a limitless supply of such stories, in part because it seems as if Dershowitz initiates a fair number of confrontations himself. The week before our conversation, he had returned to the hallowed cultural battleground of the Pierogi Wars, the West Tisbury farmers’ market. He was wearing his U.S.-Israel shirt (or “my Zionist T-shirt,” of which he has two—one red, one blue) and saw a guy wearing a Free Palestine shirt. “I walked up to him. I said, ‘Can we take a picture together?’” The man refused. “He said, ‘No, no, no Israel,’ and he walked away.” Dershowitz believes that many of his old Vineyard friends revile him for calling out the “anti-Zionist” and “radical” bent of the progressive left. He showed me his phone and cued up what he calls “my daily love note.” This one was an unsolicited email he’d just received, with “GENOCIDAL ZIONIST ISRAEL!” in the subject line; he kindly forwarded the note to me. “They always combine Zionism with pedophilia,” Dershowitz observed of his correspondents. A few times during our conversation, I questioned Dershowitz about whether people really reject him because of his Zionist views or whether it might involve something more comprehensive: him being Alan Dershowitz. His position on the Middle East seems farther down the list of reasons that people might not like him than his affiliations with Trump and Epstein and his overall reputation, accrued over decades. But Dershowitz claims, for instance, that he’s no longer asked to speak at the Martha’s Vineyard Book Festival because “they censor anybody they disagree with.” (A spokesperson for the book festival told me in an email that Dershowitz’s claim is “completely false” and that “the festival line up over the past two decades hardly reflects a narrow or excluding agenda.”) “I personify what the woke hates,” Dershowitz said. Before I could ask him what, exactly, “the woke” is, he explained that he is now seen as a “traitor” to the Democratic Party. The enmity is mutual. In September, he has a new book coming out called Why I Quit the Dems: And So Should You! The subtitle is Confessions of a Reluctant Republican . I asked Dershowitz directly whether he had voted for Trump in 2024. “You’re allowed to ask it,” he said. “And my wife does not allow me to answer it.” “Okay, so you’re going to hide behind your wife,” I said. “I’m going to hide behind my wife,” he confirmed. For the record, Dershowitz added that he always votes, and said that he had not voted for Kamala Harris. Also, his new book includes a blurb from President Trump (who obviously read every word). Alan Dershowitz watches as Donald Trump speaks to the media at Manhattan Criminal Court in May 2024. (Michael M. Santiago / Getty) Despite all of this, Dershowitz has arrived at a nuanced take on his snubbing. “I think it’s selective cancellation,” he told me. “We decided, basically, to change our life on the Vineyard.” He said that he keeps busy by writing and doing regular paid appearances on Newsmax, occasional hits on Fox News, Piers Morgan’s show on YouTube, and other outlets. (He used to be on CNN all the time, but no more—“CNN has canceled me.”) He said that he does not lack social options. He has become very active in a Vineyard Chabad that he helped start. He told me at one point about all of the new friends he’s made. “Most of them are more supportive of Israel than the other group was,” he said. “And I often ask myself, How did I allow myself to become part of that other group? ” When I asked Dershowitz who his new friends are, we wound up talking about someone who is definitely in the “other group”: Larry David. They used to speak all the time, Dershowitz told me. They would have dinner, share jokes. “I allowed him to use my gym to work out,” Dershowitz said. “I helped him on a number of occasions.” “Larry David doesn’t talk to me anymore,” Dershowitz said at another point. “He screams and yells at me when he sees me.” He told me that he used to be a fan of Curb Your Enthusiasm but can no longer bring himself to watch it. When discussing David, Dershowitz often spoke in the present tense, describing their breach as if it were an active feud and a still-fresh wound. Predictably, David had minimal enthusiasm for discussing any of this when I reached out to him. “ I don’t know why he’s still thinking and talking about me,” he told me by email. As for the five-year-old confrontation at the Chilmark store, David added this: “I have lots of confrontations on my show but rarely in life,” he said. “And then only if I think I can take them in a fight. Hence the Dershowitz dust-up.” W hile Dershowitz and I spoke on the porch, a woman sitting in a rocking chair next to him kept leaning in, almost certainly eavesdropping. She confirmed this about half an hour into our conversation. “I’m sorry to interrupt,” the woman said to Dershowitz. “I was just sitting here. And I just wanted to say, you sound super fascinating. And I hope nobody’s ever mean to you. Ever.” Dershowitz kvelled. “Did you plant her there or something?” I joked (sort of). “I only paid her 10 dollars,” he joked (I think). During our conversation, Dershowitiz told me about a less cordial episode that had taken place last month in front of the Chilmark store, just a few feet from where we were sitting. The incident was not covered in the media, but Dershowitz had filmed a portion of it on his phone and shared the video with me. A guy in a Yankees cap had spotted Dershowitz at the store and promptly launched a barrage of Bronx cheers his way from the parking lot. The man showed exemplary message discipline. “Do you defend pedophiles? Do you defend pedophiles?” he repeated. “Yes, he does.” Dershowitz demanded that his tormentor identify himself. “My name is Jeffrey Epstein Jr., great friend to Alan Dershowitz,” the man replied. Dershowitz kept demanding that the man state his name. “What are you going to do?” the man asked. “I’m going to sue you if you give your name,” Dershowitz said. (Surprisingly, the man continued to withhold his name.) “Why? What are you going to sue me for?” he asked. “For defamation.” The heckler also mocked Dershowitz for, among other things, claiming to a TV reporter that, although he’d once received a massage from an adult woman at Epstein’s house, he’d kept his underwear on during the experience. “He was on the plane, and he kept his underwear on,” the man taunted, while retreating across the street. There was some more hollering back and forth. “You’re still a schmuck,” Dershowitz shouted. In the pantheon of rogues and sleazeballs that Dershowitz has represented, Epstein stands out. Dershowitz helped orchestrate the late sex offender’s controversial plea deal in 2008; Epstein was allowed to plead guilty to state prostitution crimes in Florida, but he avoided federal trafficking charges and wound up serving just 13 months in jail. (At the time of his death, in 2019, he was awaiting trial on federal charges of child sex trafficking, by which point Dershowitz had fallen out with him and was no longer representing him.) Earlier in their relationship, they were frequent companions. Dershowitz was a visitor to Epstein’s homes in Palm Beach and New York, and went once with his wife and daughter to Epstein’s infamous island. (“No young women there,” Dershowitz wrote to me by email. “No one there except staff and ghislaine Maxwell.”) I asked Dershowitz whether he’d ever been a passenger on Epstein’s plane. “Oh, 20 times,” he said. As Epstein’s attorney, he explained, when he had to travel to Florida, his client would fly him down. However, the heckler’s claim that Dershowitz had received a massage on the plane was incorrect. That had taken place at Epstein’s home in Palm Beach. “This was a shoulder-and-neck massage, from an older woman,” Dershowitz told me. He said that this was “the only massage I’ve ever had in Epstein’s situation.” “I’ve never in my life had an erotic massage. Not even from my wife,” he added, excruciatingly. Dershowitz has said repeatedly that he never witnessed or participated in any unlawful sexual impropriety related to Epstein. In 2014, the Epstein survivor Virginia Giuffre alleged in court documents that the financier had trafficked her to multiple men while she was a minor. This included Dershowitz, who vehemently denied the charges. Giuffre sued Dershowitz for defamation, and Dershowitz countersued, claiming that she had made up the accusations. Giuffre withdrew her suit against Dershowitz in 2022, acknowledging that she might have made a mistake in identifying him. She died by suicide last year. [ Gilad Edelman: What everyone assumes about Jeffrey Epstein ] “I wish I never met him,” Dershowitz told me, speaking of Epstein. “But I don’t regret my representation of him.” This struck me as a classic bit of Dershowitz hairsplitting, and I was not quite sure what to make of it. Regardless, Dershowitz conveyed far more remorse over representing Epstein than I heard him express about any of his other clients. And he told me that he is resigned to Epstein being a lasting stain on his reputation and legacy. “I’ve been already told I will have a bad obituary in The New York Times ,” he volunteered. “Who told you that?” I asked. “Do they work at The New York Times ?” “No,” Dershowitz said. He claimed to have heard it “from a guy who does obituaries for another newspaper.” (Apparently, all obit writers swap notes.) He added that an obituary writer for the Times did call him. “With his deep obituary voice,” he noted, affecting a stentorian baritone. “I have to tell you that your obituary will include the allegations against you from Jeffrey Epstein,” the Times reporter said, according to the deep-voiced Dershowitz. He said that he’d urged the obit guy to “put it in perspective.” (Danielle Rhoades Ha, a New York Times spokesperson, declined to comment on any specific obituaries but told me by email, “We don’t write ‘negative’ or ‘positive’ obituaries, but strive for fair, comprehensive and accurate accounts of a person’s full life.”) Tony Luong for The Atlantic Dershowitz wanted to make clear to me how unfair he believes the Epstein-related allegations against him are. He and his wife have been married for 40 years, he said: “I have never cheated. I have never hugged—I don’t hug people. I don’t like hugging.” He also told me that he is “not a big massage person.” “And by the way, nobody on the Vineyard believed this, even the people who hated me,” Dershowitz added. “Because they all see me with my wife.” He went further. “In fact, the lawyer for Virginia Giuffre, he came over to me one day”—it was during a deposition—“and said, ‘Alan, I’ve seen you with your wife. I can’t believe you would ever have done anything.’” I said I was dubious that the opposing lawyer would say something like this. “I’ll give you his name—his name is Chuck Cooper.” Reached by phone for comment, Charles Cooper, Giuffre’s lawyer, told me the exchange that Dershowitz had described had never taken place. “This event that he’s reporting and this comment that he’s attributing to me are both categorically untrue,” Cooper said. He added that he remembers seeing Dershowitz with his wife on only one occasion, and that it was enough for him to make only a “fleeting observation.” Either way, “I did not say and I would never have said what he’s attributed to me,” Cooper said. “Give me a break.” I n the course of my discussion with Dershowitz, I learned of another fundamental change to his life, one that filled me with something I did not expect to feel: pathos. Last year, Dershowitz’s son Elon died at 64, after suffering a stroke. He had been diagnosed with a malignant brain tumor when he was 10 and had been told that he’d be lucky to make it to his bar mitzvah. “We took extraordinary steps,” Dershowitz said, “all over the world.” Elon had been his father’s sidekick. A film producer, he was the prime mover behind Reversal of Fortune , the 1990 legal thriller based on Dershowitz’s book about his successful defense of the British socialite Claus von Bülow in his trial for the attempted murder of his wife. The film solidified the status of Dershowitz (played by Ron Silver) as one of the “super lawyers” of his generation. “We went to the Oscars together,” Dershowitz said of him and Elon. Jeremy Irons won Best Actor for his portrayal of von Bülow. They went to an after-party. “I sat next to Gregory Peck, and it was a great moment,” Dershowitz said. When Dershowitz spoke about Elon, I detected a note of anguish in his voice. On the Vineyard, they’d been pretty much inseparable. Dershowitz’s son used to join him at the Chilmark store, when he still held court. “He would come to the porch with me every day,” Dershowitz said. If anyone came up and started giving him trouble, Elon would get after them. “He was my guy.” [ Read: Nantucket doesn’t belong to the preppies ] Everybody on the Vineyard liked Elon, Dershowitz said: “Even when they turned against me, they generally didn’t turn against Elon.” “Although Larry David did.” “Even when my son died—and Larry knew him very well—he never sent me a card,” Dershowitz said. “Never called me, never did anything to acknowledge it.” After I returned from the Vineyard, I spoke with Dershowitz by phone. Since my visit, he’d suffered a fractured rib. When I asked how it had happened, he lamented that the cause was nothing dramatic. “I mean, I’d love to have a great story,” he said. “Passionate lovemaking, you know?” (Although definitely not an erotic massage.) Alas. “I sneezed too hard,” he said. “My doctor told me at my age, a sneeze or a hard cough can fracture a rib.” Despite being in pain, Dershowitz said that he was planning to go that night to a Chabad event at the home of the billionaire hedge-fund manager Paul Singer, a big Republican donor and supporter of Israel. In a few days, Dershowitz was scheduled to be honored at the Chabad to mark the 75th anniversary of his bar mitzvah. We briefly revisited the Pierogi Incident; he sent me a link to a Facebook post from someone marking “the anniversary of Pierogigate” and vowing to “have a potato pierogi later today in honor of Dershowitz.” When I mentioned Larry David’s name again, Dershowitz sounded freshly pained—as if I’d elbowed him in his bad rib. They had been really good friends, he reiterated. I asked whether he’d had any interaction with David since the Chilmark-store episode in 2021. Not really, Dershowitz said, except for one chance meeting at a restaurant, in which David had again blown him off. Later, Dershowitz wanted to know whether I’d spoken with David for this story. After our initial email exchange, I finally did speak with David by phone late last week. He was on vacation on Martha’s Vineyard, and I expected him to be cantankerous and annoyed—which he was at first. When I brought up the matter of Elon’s death, however, David’s tone shifted. “He’s 100 percent right,” David told me, referring to Dershowitz. “I should have reached out, and I certainly regret not doing so. As I said on Curb once, ‘I think of nice things. I just don’t act on them.’” David, who turned 79 last month, said that he has been “softening” and might be open to some kind of rapprochement with Dershowitz, if only to extinguish their one-way feud once and for all. “I’m starting to feel a little sorry for him, actually,” David told me. “Certainly because of his son.” It was a touching moment, and seemed sincere. But something also felt off, as if the network had enlisted focus groups and then ordered up a feel-good ending. Then David sent me an email the next morning. “I’m loath to say anything mean because he’s been so ostracized,” he wrote of Dershowitz. A reversion to sarcasm! “But he only has himself to blame. He made a deal with the devil. Literally. And I’d bet the devil hasn’t said a word to him since the impeachment.”

items.title: Super Eagles players who have joined new clubs this summer (Full list)
items.description: By Enitan Abdultawab A lot of Super Eagles stars have switched clubs during the 2026 summer transfer window, with Nigerian players taking on new challenges across Europe. Taiwo Awoniyi’s move to Coventry City is the latest in a series of transfers involving prominent members of the national team. The Nigerian forward completed his move from Nottingham Forest to Coventry City in a deal reportedly worth £17 million, ending his four-year spell at the City Ground. Awoniyi is one of several Nigerian internationals who have sought new challenges this summer, with players moving across England, Germany, Turkey and other European leagues. Here is the list of Super Eagles stars who have joined new clubs this summer: Kelechi Iheanacho Kelechi Iheanacho left Scottish champions Celtic after a successful spell with the club, where he contributed to their Premiership and Scottish Cup triumphs. Despite initially agreeing to a one-year contract with an option for another season, Celtic reportedly opted not to continue with the Nigerian forward. He has now joined Turkish side Bursaspor. Taiwo Awoniyi Awoniyi ended his four-year association with Nottingham Forest after completing a permanent transfer to newly promoted Coventry City. The striker endured an inconsistent spell at Forest but remained an influential figure within the dressing room. His move to Coventry is expected to provide him with an opportunity for more regular playing time as the club prepares for life in the Premier League under Frank Lampard. Akor Adams Akor Adams has begun a new chapter in Italy after completing a permanent move from Sevilla to Serie A side Venezia. The Nigerian striker signed a contract with Venezia until June 2030, with the Italian club confirming his arrival on July 22. Adams joined Sevilla in January 2025 and scored 10 goals and provided four assists in 37 appearances for the Spanish club before making the switch to Italy Raphael Onyedika Raphael Onyedika brought his time at Belgian club Club Brugge to an end after establishing himself as an important midfielder during his spell in Belgium. The Super Eagles midfielder had attracted interest from clubs in Turkey, England and Saudi Arabia before eventually opting for a move to Germany. Onyedika joined Eintracht Frankfurt, where he will look to continue his development and make an impact in the Bundesliga. The midfielder will also hope to follow in the footsteps of Nigerian football legend Austin ‘Jay-Jay’ Okocha, who previously represented the German club. Gift Orban Gift Orban has also moved on this summer after a difficult spell at Italian club Hellas Verona. The forward, who was on loan from Hoffenheim, reportedly had disciplinary issues during his time in Italy, including a reported confrontation with a fan. Orban has now joined newly promoted Turkish Super League side Amedspor on loan as he looks to revive his career and rediscover the form that made him one of Nigeria’s most exciting young forwards. Frank Onyeka Frank Onyeka has completed a permanent move to Coventry City after initially joining the club on loan from Brentford. The midfielder played an important role in Coventry’s promotion campaign, helping the club recover from a difficult period during the season. His loan agreement reportedly contained a clause requiring Coventry to make the transfer permanent if they secured promotion to the Premier League. That condition was activated following their promotion. Chidozie Awaziem Experienced defender Chidozie Awaziem is another Nigerian international who has moved clubs this summer. Awaziem joined Turkish side Konyaspor from French Ligue 1 club Nantes, returning to Turkey after previously spending time at Caykur Rizespor on loan in 2019. His move comes amid increased interest in the Turkish league among Nigerian players. Leon Balogun Former Super Eagles defender Leon Balogun has also begun a new chapter in his career. The 38-year-old left Cypriot club Aris Limassol and joined Hungarian side ETO Gyor. Balogun, who has enjoyed a lengthy career across several European leagues, will now look to contribute his experience during the latter stages of his playing career. The post Super Eagles players who have joined new clubs this summer (Full list) appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Nayala: la CEB de Toma célèbre l’excellence scolaire avec 98,31 % de réussite au CEP
items.description: BURKINA-NAYALA-EXCELLENCE-SCOLAIRE Nayala: la CEB de Toma célèbre l’excellence scolaire avec 98,31 % de réussite au CEP Toma, 16 août 2026 (AIB) – La Circonscription d’éducation de base (CEB) de Toma a célébré, samedi à toma, sa première Journée de l’excellence scolaire, au cours de laquelle des prix ont été remis aux meilleurs élèves, enseignants et écoles, ainsi qu’à l’école la plus résiliente et aux structures ayant contribué aux réformes éducatives. Cette célébration vient consacrer les performances enregistrées par la CEB de Toma, avec 98,31 % de réussite au Certificat d’études primaires (CEP) et 100 % à l’entrée en sixième. La cérémonie s’est déroulée s’est en présence des autorités communales, administratives coutumières et religieuses, des forces de défense et de sécurité, des acteurs et des partenaires de l’éducation ainsi que des parents d’élèves, et des lauréats Le directeur provincial de l’éducation préscolaire, primaire et non formelle du Nayala, Thomas Garané, a relevé que la CEB de Toma a enregistré la meilleure performance provinciale au CEP, avec 924 candidats présentés et 98,31 % de réussite. Il a également salué le taux de 100 % enregistré à l’entrée en sixième, ainsi que la performance d’une enseignante ayant obtenu 100 % de réussite avec 80 candidats présentés. Le président de la délégation spéciale de la commune de Toma, Zakaria Sawadogo a appelé à inscrire cette célébration dans la durée. « L’excellence, la célébrer aujourd’hui, c’est en faire une culture permanente », a-t-il affirmé, rappelant que l’éducation constitue une responsabilité partagée entre la famille, l’école, la communauté et les pouvoirs publics. Le chef de la CEB de Toma, Bruno Ky, a indiqué que cette première édition constitue une reconnaissance du mérite et du travail accompli. Il a salué l’engagement des enseignants, des encadreurs pédagogiques, des parents et des communautés éducatives, tout en souhaitant que cette initiative devienne un rendez-vous annuel de valorisation des bonnes pratiques. Le parrain, le commandant Ousseni Zida, a exhorté les élèves à maintenir leurs efforts et à faire de l’apprentissage un moyen de mieux servir la nation. « Le plus dur n’est pas d’être meilleur, mais d’être constant », a-t-il insisté. La cérémonie s’est achevée par une plantation d’arbres offerts par le parrain. La CEB de Toma entend poursuivre cette dynamique afin de mobiliser l’ensemble des acteurs autour de l’éducation et d’en faire une priorité pour la construction d’un avenir meilleur. Agence d’Information du Burkina KTA/bak

items.title: The Galamsey war and GWL’s fictitious and inaccurate rebuttal
items.description: The Ghana Water Limited (GWL) has assembled a collection of fictitious and inaccurate information in an attempt to dispute comments I made on PMExpress on JoyNews regarding access to water turbidity data. The Fiction In its statement of 17 August 2026, signed by its Managing Director, GWL asserted that it is “totally untrue that the Presidency [emphasis mine] has directed GWL to withhold river turbidity data”. That assertion is based on a fictitious and imaginary claim that I never made. I never said the Presidency was responsible for the inability of previously reliable GWL sources to provide me and my team with turbidity data. I personally spoke to a few senior sources at GWL to obtain the data. One was emphatic that he could no longer provide us with the turbidity data because he had been victimised and warned not to share it. Another promised to look into it, but when I called to follow up a few hours later, he made it clear that he would not be able to provide the data. One of the WhatsApp messages I received from a senior GWL official read: “I have been personally told to stay away from talking about galamsey. If I ask for this figure, it may bring me a problem later.” So, was I told that the turbidity data could not be shared because of fear of victimisation and direct warnings against sharing it? The answer is an emphatic YES! Was I told that the Presidency had directed GWL to withhold river turbidity data? The answer is an emphatic NO! Did I attribute the inability of senior GWL staff to provide the turbidity data to a presidential directive? Again, the answer is an emphatic NO! What I said—and what I stand by—was: “Today, when we tried checking, we realised that everybody else in Ghana Water Company told us something very clearly. They were very frank with us: ‘We can no longer give you the data because we’ve been told not to.’” The assertion attributed to me in the GWL statement signed by its Managing Director is pure fiction. More Fiction Point 3 of the statement also asserted that “according to official records, Mr Evans Mensah did not visit the Kwanyako plant”. I never asserted anywhere on PMExpress that I visited the Kwanyako plant. I called my regular contacts among senior staff and managers at GWL for the information. Again, that point in the statement was a response to a fictitious and imaginary claim that I never made. I have attached the video of what I actually said. The Tragedy The real tragedy of the GWL statement is its strenuous effort to major in a minor—and a loudly misleading minor at that—in the face of the grave existential threat posed by galamsey, or illegal mining. The statement had five main points, three of which were devoted to denying responsibility for recording and holding turbidity data. GWL claims that it only conducts turbidity tests during treatment to determine when to shut down plants after levels exceed safe thresholds. It then concludes that “the responsibility for managing and monitoring river bodies and holding turbidity data lies with the Water Resources Commission (WRC) and the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).” So, does GWL record turbidity data or not? The answer is an emphatic YES! Its own statement admits it. Whether the data is recorded on river bodies or at the headworks of its treatment plants is a red herring. In any case, my comments on PMExpress were in direct reference to turbidity data recorded at the Kwanyako Water Treatment Plant. So, what exactly was GWL attempting to clarify? The bottom line is that GWL records and holds turbidity data. It is that simple, and no attempt to mislead the public will alter this fact. This is especially important when we are talking about galamsey, the greatest threat to our collective survival as a people. GWL cannot be allowed to trivialise the matter. The Evidence GWL’s own evidence exposes the mischief in its statement. Below is the official record of what GWL calls the “Water Quality Assurance Coagulation Test”, conducted on the Ayensu River [emphasis mine] at the Kwanyako Headworks. It is, therefore, palpably false to claim that “GWL does not hold official data on natural river bodies”. GWL not only holds official data on river bodies and the quality of the water at its plants, but has also shared that data with JoyNews before. On 6 September 2025, a team of JoyNews reporters visited the Kwanyako Headworks following GWL’s decision to shut it down because of unsafe turbidity levels caused by the activities of illegal miners. GWL officers on site took the time to share with the JoyNews team turbidity records dating back to 2016, when turbidity was as low as 25 Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU) . When we visited on 6 September last year, the turbidity level had risen to a catastrophic 94,800 NTU . The evidence is contained in our recorded interaction with GWL officers at the Kwanyako Water Treatment Plant. The evidence is clear: GWL has shared turbidity data with JoyNews before, as recently as September 2025. So why is it that, all of a sudden, GWL’s Managing Director is pointing to the WRC and EPA for turbidity data that GWL obviously has? Is it because GWL no longer wants to share its turbidity data? Would that explain why the senior officers I spoke to were unwilling to oblige, as they had so readily done just a year ago? In fact, in 2024, GWL itself officially released turbidity data. On 30 August 2024, GWL issued a statement in which it formally reported the turbidity level of the Pra River, particularly within the catchment from which the Sekyere Hemang Water Treatment Plant abstracts water. It did so following a dangerously high turbidity reading of 14,000 NTU, which made it impossible to supply water to several communities in the Central Region. I have reproduced that statement below to substantiate the point. Again, it is factually inaccurate for GWL to suggest that it bears no responsibility for monitoring river bodies and that “the responsibility for … monitoring river bodies lies with the Water Resources Commission (WRC) and the Environmental Protection Agency”. The Managing Director of GWL himself is on record as having authorised the deployment of drone technology to monitor river bodies for pollution by illegal miners. During a working visit to the Kwanyako Water Treatment Plant in September 2025, he was quoted as saying: “We cannot just report that turbidity is high without clear evidence of where the pollution is coming from. With drone surveillance, we can identify whether illegal mining or other activities are to blame.” The fact that the WRC and EPA may have primary responsibility does not mean that GWL has no responsibility. What is clear to me is that GWL’s Managing Director is trying too hard to repudiate responsibility for turbidity data by making palpably misleading claims to justify doing so. The galamsey war is simply too important to trivialise. As part of its contribution to that war, GWL must be transparent by publishing turbidity data from its treatment plants, as it did in August 2024 and September 2025.
